title: Welcome to the Garden
subtitle: Moving day. The community, already made — and how it works.

customObject.name: the commons board
customObject.description: a wide wooden board hung with softly glowing slips — the work the place thinks it needs

script.note: Moving day. Morning in a garden between small houses — his friend walking beside him, four doors from her own. A wide wooden board hangs between two posts, dressed in glowing slips of paper.

script.text: The map said this area's called the Garden. Who named it that?

The people living here did — every area names itself. This one reached back twenty-three centuries for it: a man bought a cheap house outside the city, brought his friends to live near, and made sure everyone had something to do.
A home you can afford. Friends close by. Work worth doing. We didn't invent the three things — we just stopped pretending they were optional.

script.note: An older man is pinning a fresh slip to the board. It brightens under his hand.

script.text: Morning. You're the new pair of hands? Board's fresh — best time to look.
Everything this place thinks it needs, posted by whoever noticed it. You pick what you feel is needed — nobody assigns you. It pays in what we have. Sometimes money. Always standing.
Anyone can post? So if I see something wrong here, I don't file a complaint with somebody who never visits —
You post it. Or you fix it, and post that you fixed it. Power over what's around you — that's half of what peace is.

The houses came the same way. We told the design engines what we could spend and how we wanted to live — near each other, small, warm — and they drew a hundred versions until one felt like ours. Nobody here lives in lack. Lack was a design fault.

script.note: A soft bell. The garden stills. No one gathers — each settles where they are: a porch, a bench, a room of their own.

script.text: The quiet hour — each of us in our own place. You settle the body, take the mind off the noise, and put it on the life you intend — grateful for it, before breakfast. Some call it meditation, some call it prayer. No one is graded, and no one is gathered.
You all really believe this holds? A place run on noticing things and sitting quietly?
It holds the way a garden holds — by devotion. You give it your thought, you accept living in a place that was made for it, and it feeds you back. Skip the devotion and it's just housing.

This place was made for the ones who fell through the gaps of normal society — and for the ones who were looking for more. It will bring all of you to a new understanding and value of life. A vision that inspires you to live on planet earth.
All of me. …Where do I start?

script.note: He lifts a slip from the board. It brightens in his hand.
